meta.objective: Participants can write effective prompts for campaign copy using a structured framework

slides.title: Welcome: Prompt Engineering for Marketers
bullets: What you will be able to do after today
Agenda overview
Ground rules and questions

notes.aim: Set expectations and create psychological safety for non-technical participants.
notes.instructions: Open with a show-of-hands: who has tried ChatGPT before? Acknowledge all levels.
notes.reflective_q: What is one thing you hope to take away from today?
notes.debrief: Recap the learning objective and confirm the agenda is clear before moving on.

slides.title: What Is a Prompt and Why Does It Matter?
bullets: A prompt is an instruction to an AI model
The quality of the output depends on the quality of the input
Three core elements: role, task, context

notes.aim: Give participants a mental model for how prompts work.
notes.instructions: Walk through each element with a whiteboard example. Use marketing scenarios.
notes.reflective_q: Can you think of a task you do weekly where this model might apply?
notes.debrief: Summarise: role tells the AI who to be, task tells it what to do, context tells it what you know.

slides.title: The Prompt Framework: Role – Task – Context – Format
bullets: Role: 'You are a senior copywriter for a luxury brand'
Task: 'Write a 3-sentence Instagram caption'
Context: 'Product launch for summer collection, tone is aspirational'
Format: 'Return only the caption, no explanation'

rows: What does it need to know?

notes.aim: Make the framework concrete and memorable with a visual table.
notes.instructions: Show the table slide, then demo live in ChatGPT using the exact example.
notes.reflective_q: Which element do you think is most often missing in prompts you have tried?
notes.debrief: Format is often forgotten — it dramatically changes output length and usefulness.

slides.title: Real Example: Before and After
bullets: BEFORE: 'Write something about our new product'
AFTER: 'You are a senior copywriter. Write a 3-sentence Instagram caption for our summer collection launch. Tone: aspirational. Return only the caption.'
Result: specific, on-brand, usable output

notes.aim: Show the concrete difference the framework makes on a realistic marketing task.
notes.instructions: Run both prompts live. Show outputs side by side. Let participants react.
notes.reflective_q: What is the first thing you notice about the difference in output quality?
notes.debrief: Specificity is not about more words — it is about the right words in the right places.

slides.title: Your Turn: Write a Prompt for a Real Campaign
bullets: Choose a task from your current campaign backlog
Apply the Role – Task – Context – Format framework
Run your prompt and evaluate the output
Pair up and compare: what worked, what did not?

notes.aim: Apply the framework to a real task each participant already owns.
notes.instructions: Give 15 min solo, then 10 min paired comparison. Circulate and ask questions. Save 5 min for 2–3 pairs to share.
notes.reflective_q: What would you change about your prompt based on what your pair showed you?
notes.debrief: There is rarely one right answer — iteration is the skill. The framework gives you a starting point.

slides.title: Key Takeaways and Next Steps
bullets: Every prompt has four elements: role, task, context, format
Specificity beats length — precision matters more than detail
Iteration is the skill — your first prompt is a draft
This week: use the framework on one real work task

notes.aim: Consolidate learning and give participants a clear immediate action.
notes.instructions: Ask 2–3 participants to share their biggest insight. Close with the next-steps ask.
notes.reflective_q: What is the one thing you will try differently in your next AI interaction?
notes.debrief: End on action, not summary. Participants leave with a task, not just knowledge.

prebite:
## Before the Session

**Read (10 min):** [How to Write Better AI Prompts](https://example.com) — or search 'prompt engineering basics' and read any short article.

**Try (5 min):** Open ChatGPT or Claude and ask it to write a social media post for a product you know. Notice what you like and dislike about the result. Bring your example to the session.

**Reflect:** What tasks in your current role are mostly writing or summarising? Come with one real example in mind.
postbite:
## After the Session

**Assignment (this week):** Apply the Role–Task–Context–Format framework to one real work task. Screenshot your prompt and the output.

**Reflection questions:**
1. What surprised you most about how the AI responded to a well-structured prompt?
2. Where did the output still fall short, and what would you add to the context next time?
3. Which of your regular tasks could benefit most from prompt engineering?

**Further reading:**
- OpenAI Prompt Engineering Guide: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/prompt-engineering
- Anthropic's Claude prompting tips: https://docs.anthropic.com/claude/docs/prompt-engineering
